title: One press can deliver two events: a textEvent, then a sysEvent
claim: The handle-input skill says a press on a text container arrives as a sysEvent. No official material mentions a second event for the same press.
actual: Reports disagree. One report on G2 hardware with SDK 0.0.13 sees, for every press, the text container's click event with no eventType at once, then a sysEvent about 350 ms later. Another report on SDK 0.0.14 and Even App 2.2.10 logged nine taps on hardware and got nine sysEvent payloads and no textEvent.
impact: Where both events arrive, a handler that reads either envelope acts twice on one press: a toggle starts and stops at once. A debounce on one path does not help, because the second event comes on the other.
workaround: Debounce presses across textEvent and sysEvent together, not per envelope. The first reporter ignores any press within 1.2 s of the previous one.

evidence.note: Measured on hardware 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-09. Even App 2.2.x, minor version not given. Server logs showed recordings stopped at once by the second event.
Nine taps on hardware gave nine sysEvent payloads and no textEvent. Simulator on macOS 15.
One text container with isEventCapture 1. Each click delivered one sysEvent and nothing else. Same on SDK 0.0.14. The simulator may differ from hardware here.
